clips.text_zh: /biz/ 又有人話 Doge 3日後上太空，叫人小注 all-in。講到尾都係咪要避下 SNL 2.0。btw 我嘅倉都係得個吉，睇下佢今次點表演。lol 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to space in 3 days and you are not buying. If this shit explodes it will still move up, so why not ape a bit, then sell so it does not become SNL 2.0. Or maybe it will just start the hype again.
clips.source_hint: biz thread hyping an imminent Dogecoin catalyst

signal.rationale: OP suggests a small speculative long around the space launch event

clips.text_en_b2: Doge is heading to space in roughly three days, and hardly anyone is buying in. Even if the whole thing flops it will likely pump a little, so throwing in a modest position makes sense, then unloading before it turns into another SNL-style disaster. Then again, it could simply kick the hype cycle back into gear.
clips.text_en_c1: Doge is purportedly heading to space within the next 72 hours, yet retail sentiment remains tepid. Should the launch prove spectacular, even a modest position could yield substantial upside, whereas a complete miss would inevitably invite comparisons with the infamous SNL 2.0 debacle. The calculus, therefore, favours a calculated entry followed by disciplined profit-taking before sentiment sours. My own exposure is negligible, so this is largely a spectator's wager, but the spectacle itself could reignite momentum. Markets, after all, thrive on narrative as much as on fundamentals.
clips.text_en_c2: The Dogecoin spectacle reaches its next inflection point in roughly seventy-two hours, when, ostensibly, a payload bearing the meme-coin's insignia departs for low-Earth orbit. Speculators on the board are urging a measured position rather than wholesale conviction, the rationale being that even a modest catalyst ought to translate into upward momentum. The operative concern, however, remains tail risk: the asset's SNL-era rout lingers as cautionary precedent, and any subsequent rally risks being repriced as theatrical flourish rather than substantive demand. Having been thoroughly marginalised by prior cycles, my own exposure amounts to little more than nominal presence. I intend to observe proceedings with the resigned detachment of a spectator who has, on previous occasions, mistaken the carnival for the market.

clips.text_zh: Saudi 東西輸油管被炸，估計要 6 至 12 個月先維修到。但係今日油價反而跌。又係學費。wtf 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Big happening: 150 dollar oil soon? The Saudi east-west pipeline got hit. So the Saudis can no longer go around the Strait of Hormuz. This is the only pipeline from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea. The satellite pic shows fire damage in multiple places and a pump station is rumored hit. AI repair estimate: 6 to 12 months.
clips.source_hint: biz thread on a geopolitical oil supply shock

signal.rationale: OP expects oil to spike to 150 USD on a multi-month supply disruption, which historically supports gold as a safe haven

clips.text_en_b2: Looks like a genuine catalyst for $150 oil could be on the horizon. Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline just took a hit, which means they can no longer bypass the Strait of Hormuz. It remains the sole conduit from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea, and satellite imagery reportedly shows fire damage at several points, with one pump station possibly compromised. Forecasts suggest repairs could take anywhere from six to twelve months, and Saudi Arabia still accounts for around ten percent of global supply.
clips.text_en_c1: A significant development has emerged: the Saudi East-West pipeline has reportedly sustained substantial damage, with satellite imagery indicating fire damage across multiple sections and at least one pump station allegedly compromised. Should this assessment hold, repairs would necessitate a six-to-twelve-month window, effectively eliminating the Persian Gulf's only viable bypass of the Strait of Hormuz. Given that Saudi Arabia accounts for approximately ten percent of global crude production, the geopolitical ramifications should be considerable. Paradoxically, oil prices declined today, a reminder that markets frequently reward contrarian interpretations over obvious catalysts.
clips.text_en_c2: A strike on Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline has effectively severed the kingdom's principal terrestrial bypass of the Strait of Hormuz, which had hitherto constituted the sole conduit ferrying crude from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea. Satellite imagery corroborates the damage, revealing thermal scarring across multiple segments, while unverified reports suggest a pumping station has likewise been compromised. Independent assessments converge on a remediation horizon of between six and twelve months, a timeline whose geopolitical ramifications are difficult to overstate given that the kingdom accounts for roughly a tenth of global supply. Curiously, however, the spot market responded with an emphatic sell-off, a counterintuitive dislocation that seasoned participants have wryly characterised as yet another instalment in the tuition of speculative literacy.

clips.text_zh: 今日又睇 slope，諗下 factor of safety 同 soil nail 點擺。考牌都未溫完，靠 AI 續命 ok。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: I'm a civil engineer working on slope surveys and GI reports. Today I was checking soil nailing layout and drainage for a contractor. Half the time I am computing factor of safety by hand, the other half I am arguing with Tommy about bar spacing. Studying for the FE exam after work, so basically running on coffee and vibes.
clips.source_hint: biz life-story thread adapted to slope/soil nail context

signal.rationale: No trade, just engineer's daily reality

clips.text_en_b2: I'm a civil engineer currently handling slope inspections and drafting geotechnical interpretive reports. Today I spent the bulk of it reviewing soil nailing configurations and drainage provisions for a contractor, although half the time I was crunching factor of safety calculations manually while debating bar spacing with Tommy. I am also cramming for the FE exam after hours, basically fuelled by caffeine and sheer stubbornness.
clips.text_en_c1: I am a civil engineer currently engaged in slope stability assessments and ground investigation reports. Today's responsibilities included verifying soil nailing configurations and reviewing drainage provisions for an external contractor. The workload bifurcates rather predictably: half of it involves manually computing factors of safety, the other half consists of protracted negotiations with Tommy over bar spacing tolerances. Following office hours, I attempt to study for the Fundamentals of Engineering examination, though retention remains marginal. The regimen persists on caffeine and whatever professional credibility remains intact.
clips.text_en_c2: The exigencies of a slope-stability assignment once again consumed the working day, with particular attention devoted to soil-nail layout, subsoil drainage, and the iterative computation of factors of safety that remain, regrettably, a manual affair for the foreseeable future. A protracted exchange with a contractor regarding bar spacing consumed the afternoon, leaving me to reconcile competing assumptions and, rather more pressingly, to resume preparation for the Fundamentals of Engineering examination, which looms with all the urgency of an overdue geological survey. The customary regimen of caffeine, denial, and half-digested reference manuals has therefore resumed in earnest, supplemented, I confess, by recourse to AI tooling that performs the heavy analytical lifting my stamina cannot.

clips.text_zh: 今日睇 beam column load path，RC 同 steel design 都要 re-check。Sum Ho 何生又問點解用呢個 method。wtf，考牌書都未開 lol。👍
clips.text_en_b1: I am a civil engineer and tonight I am reviewing load path for beams and columns on a small structural job. Reinforced concrete on one side, steel design on the other. Sum Ho asked me why I picked this method and how I checked it. I just stared at the calc sheet and prayed the FE study notes kick in by Friday.
clips.source_hint: biz career-anxiety thread adapted to structural design context
clips.text_en_b2: I'm a civil engineer, and tonight I have been going over the load path for beams and columns on a fairly modest structural project. One side calls for reinforced concrete detailing while the other demands steel design checks, so everything needs re-verification. Sum Ho then asked why I had settled on this particular method and how I had validated it. I just stared at my calc sheet, silently praying my FE study notes somehow click by Friday.
clips.text_en_c1: I am a civil engineer presently reviewing load path continuity for a modest structural assignment, one half of which involves reinforced concrete detailing while the other concerns steel member design. Sum Ho, the supervising engineer, challenged my selection of analytical methodology and questioned the verification procedure employed. Confronted with his queries, I could only contemplate my calculation sheet in mute deference. Should my FE study materials prove inadequate by Friday, the consequences will be thoroughly inconvenient; preparation, regrettably, has been deferred until conditions became urgent.
clips.text_en_c2: The evening's structural review centred on a modest assignment whose load path traverses both reinforced-concrete and steel framing, each material demanding its own recondite methodology. My principal interlocutor, Sum Ho, posed the perennially uncomfortable question of why a particular analytical approach had been adopted and, more pointedly, how its assumptions might be defended under scrutiny. Confronted with a calculation sheet whose provenance I could no longer credibly defend, I resorted to the venerable tactic of appearing deliberative whilst inwardly petitioning every deity relevant to the discipline. The FE study notes remain, at present, a largely aspirational document, although I cling to the conviction that comprehension will materialise, somehow, by Friday.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 講 AI model 已經 plateau，VC 要 fake story 保住水喉。又係睇住自己行業畀 AI 食。btw 廢柴如我都驚份工 lol。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: So they are admitting AI models have plateaued and are coming up with some fake story about self restraint so they do not lose VC money. I am so tired of this talmudic bullshit. Either the next training run unlocks real gains or every AI startup is now a PowerPoint company.
clips.source_hint: g/ thread on AI scaling hitting a wall

signal.rationale: No trade, macro observation on AI capex

clips.text_en_b2: So they're openly conceding that AI models have effectively plateaued, and now they're spinning some contrived narrative about self-restraint purely to keep the VC cash flowing. I'm frankly exhausted by this kind of circular reasoning. Either the next training run delivers genuine breakthroughs or every AI startup out there is basically a PowerPoint company propped up by hype.
clips.text_en_c1: It appears the industry is finally conceding that AI models have plateaued, a development that has prompted venture capital constituents to fabricate increasingly elaborate narratives concerning self-imposed restraint, ostensibly to preserve funding pipelines. Such manoeuvres, while understandable from a fiduciary standpoint, remain intellectually exhausting. Should the subsequent training run fail to deliver substantive improvements, the prevailing sentiment suggests that numerous AI enterprises will devolve into little more than PowerPoint operations propped up by speculative capital.
clips.text_en_c2: The discourse on the technology board has converged, with uncharacteristic candour, on the proposition that frontier model development has reached a point of diminishing returns, with the much-vaunted trajectory toward general intelligence evidently flattening. In lieu of verifiable breakthroughs, capital allocators are reportedly papering over the gap with a convenient narrative of deliberate self-restraint, a rhetorical stratagem designed, so the cynicism goes, to preserve funding pipelines until the next training run delivers something tangible. As someone whose profession is being steadily subsumed by the very systems these investors underwrite, the spectacle is alternately galling and instructive. I anticipate two terminal outcomes: genuine progress, or a wholesale migration of so-called AI companies into PowerPoint consultancy.

clips.text_zh: /pol/ 問如果同中國開戰點算。HK 喺中間，真係諗下要唔要早啲走返 Florida。廢物如我，睇完都係繼續 grind lol。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: If we ever go to war with China, we are fucked, right? There is no way we can keep up with their manufacturing capacity and they have already stolen all our technology. Honestly the only safe play is to stack cash and move somewhere cheap with space, like Florida.
clips.text_en_b2: If we ever actually go to war with China, we'd be absolutely screwed. There is no realistic way we can match their manufacturing capacity, and they've already pilfered most of our proprietary technology. The only halfway sensible play seems to be stockpiling cash and relocating somewhere cheap with plenty of land, which is why I'm seriously considering Florida despite everything.
clips.text_en_c1: Should hostilities ever materialise between our respective nations and China, the strategic calculus appears rather unfavourable, given their manufacturing capacity and the considerable technological advantages they have allegedly acquired. Hong Kong's geographical positioning renders prolonged exposure untenable, prompting serious consideration of an accelerated relocation to Florida, where property remains comparatively affordable. Whether such preparations constitute prudence or mere paranoia remains debatable; regardless, the prudent course involves liquid reserves and geographic optionality, particularly when civilisational tail risks warrant contingency planning beyond conventional investment horizons.
clips.text_en_c2: The discourse on the political board contemplates, with characteristic alarmism, the prospect of open hostilities with the People's Republic, a scenario whose asymmetric industrial dimensions render protracted conflict rather unfavourable. China's manufacturing depth, compounded by what is described, with varying degrees of charity, as the systematic appropriation of Western technical knowledge, suggests that any sustained mobilisation would expose rather glaring supply-chain dependencies. For those of us lodged in geographies of evident strategic vulnerability, the calculus is grimly straightforward: liquidate illiquid positions, accumulate reserves, and consider relocation to jurisdictions whose principal attractions include affordability and acreage. Florida, for reasons defying pure reason, continues to feature prominently in these discussions.

clips.text_zh: /fit/ 有個話同 twin 食一樣但自己肥。肥仔信今晚又笑我 bench 得一塊。教我點算好。靠 AI 續命 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: I have an identical twin brother. He is lean. I am fat. We measured how much we eat and the calorie count is identical. Dietary fat, protein, and carbs are identical. We also collected our faeces and incinerated them and the calorie count is identical too. So what is actually causing me to be obese while he is lean?
clips.source_hint: fit thread on identical twins with different body composition
clips.text_en_b2: I have an identical twin brother, and here's the frustrating setup. He's lean while I'm carrying noticeable weight, despite the fact we measured our intake and the calorie totals came out identical. We tracked dietary fat, protein, and carbs down to the gram, and they matched. We even went as far as collecting and incinerating our faeces to compare, and somehow the calorie counts still aligned. So what on earth is making me obese while he stays lean?
clips.text_en_c1: I possess an identical twin brother who maintains a notably lean physique, whereas I remain considerably overweight despite ostensibly identical conditions. We have undertaken rigorous measurements of our respective caloric intake, and the figures align precisely across all macronutrient categories: fats, proteins, and carbohydrates. To eliminate digestive variables, we collected and incinerated our faecal matter, which yielded equivalent caloric values. This controlled experiment renders the disparity genuinely perplexing; if energy in equals energy out, then what mechanism accounts for my obesity relative to his leanness?
clips.text_en_c2: An unsettling proposition surfaced on the fitness board, advanced by a poster whose identical twin brother exhibits a lean physique whilst he himself carries substantial adiposity. Rigorous empirical protocol was, by his account, observed: caloric intake measured and found to be indistinguishable; macronutrient distributions verified as identical; faecal samples even collected, incinerated, and subjected to calorimetric analysis, yielding equivalent outputs. The conclusion—that dietary accounting alone cannot account for the divergence—suggests the involvement of factors beyond conscious behaviour: microbiome composition, hormonal milieu, sleep architecture, or, more darkly, genetic methylation patterns operating beneath the threshold of self-reporting. The thread has, predictably, devolved into a contest of anecdote, with bench-press one-rep-maxes offered as proxies for metabolic authority.
